notes: wowsims-forever models one Hunter spell package for all three specs; this is the spec the fork's own p1.apl.json preset is already built for (heavy Aimed Shot weaving), so it is the closest adaptation of the three hunter files. Marksmanship also keeps Serpent Sting up for the extra sustained damage, unlike Beast Mastery where community guides call it not worth a global. Every rank named here is checked against this build's own spellconst: the preset names Multi-Shot as spell 25294, which does not exist in this build (Multi-Shot only has one rank here, 2643), and calls Serpent Sting rank 8 when 25295 is actually rank 9 -- both fixed here rather than copied stale. Aimed Shot (20904) is registered by the engine again since 2026-09-28 (its registration had been commented out, and the cast line was declared inert until then). What did need fixing: nothing in this site's request pipeline (sim/request) ever sets a character's DistanceFromTarget, so every hunter starts at 0 -- inside Raptor Strike's melee range but under Multi-Shot, Serpent Sting and Aimed Shot's own ExtraCastCondition floor of 12 (core.MinRangedAttackDistance), which also gates the ranged auto-attack itself (sim/core/attack.go's startPull). A `move` prepull action to 30 yards is added so this and every future simulation of this spec actually has a ranged auto-attack and can cast its ranged abilities, matching how a Marksmanship hunter is actually played. Under this smoke build specifically (no gear equipped anywhere) the ranged weapon's SwingSpeed is the Weapon{} zero value, which collapses the ranged swing timer to its 500ms cast-time floor (sim/core/attack.go's WeaponAttack.updateSwingDuration: curSwingDuration = weapon.SwingSpeed / hasteMultiplier = 0) -- a real ranged weapon's positive SwingSpeed does not have this problem. The resulting sub-GCD auto-shot loop saturates the character's action economy so completely that the priority list, including Multi-Shot and Serpent Sting, never gets a decision window in this one bare-weapon run; this is a new engine-side artifact of the no-gear smoke build (recorded for the engine ledger), not a defect in this rotation's gates. Rotation-accuracy program diagnosis (2026-09-28): the inert ids above (Multi-Shot 2643, Rapid Fire 3045) are level-gated in the engine (sim/hunter/multi_shot.go RequiredLevel 18, sim/hunter/rapid_fire.go's registerRapidFire returns if hunter.Level < 26) but carry rank:0 rows in spellranks.json, which the ladder's idLearnLevel deliberately does not level-gate (the same skip keeps Bloodrage/Judgement -- genuinely never level-gated by the engine -- from being wrongly treated as gated); not declared inert here (both resolve fine above their real gate under the pinned engine); see hunter-beast-mastery.json's notes (the shared hunter spell package all three specs use) for the full diagnosis and the sim/internal/spellranks + sim/request/ladder.go fix that actually resolves this.

sources.label: wowsims-forever default hunter priority list, Multi-Shot and Serpent Sting ranks corrected against this build
Warcraft Tavern: Classic Marksmanship Hunter rotation (Aimed Shot / Multi-Shot weave, Serpent Sting kept up)
Forever Sixty default rotation, unvalidated until the nightly job runs

priorityList.notes: Rapid Fire timed to land with an incoming auto shot just as Aimed Shot is about to come off cooldown, so both benefit.
Aimed Shot on cooldown, timed so its cast does not clip the next auto shot.
Serpent Sting kept up whenever it is about to fall off and neither shot above is close to ready.
Multi-Shot as the filler between Aimed Shots.

Arcane Shot as the last filler, only when neither shot above will be ready within a global and mana is above the floor: it is instant, so it never clips an auto shot, but it is the least mana-efficient shot, and a Classic-length fight runs dry without the floor.
